record.paper_title: An algorithm for solving linear nonhomogeneous quaternion-valued differential equations and some open problems
record.original_question: For quaternion-valued differential equations, can one develop a theory of discontinuous systems that extends existing discontinuous control schemes—such as impulsive, switching, time-scale, piecewise, and fuzzy-system methods—to the quaternion-valued setting, and in particular determine whether discontinuous control strategies used for discontinuous ordinary differential equations can be adapted to discontinuous quaternion-valued differential equations?

evidence.quote: For the applications, it is known that several types of control schemes are proposed for the impulsive systems (e.g see [20, 25, 39]). Is it possible to extend such kinds of discontinuous control schemes to discontinuous QDEs?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}=\{a_0+a_1 i+a_2 j+a_3 k: a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3\in\mathbb{R}\}$ denote the skew field of real quaternions, with multiplication determined by $i^2=j^2=k^2=ijk=-1$. A quaternion-valued differential equation (QDE) on an interval $I\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ has the form
$$\dot x(t)=F(t,x(t)),\qquad x(t)\in\mathbb{H}^n,$$
where $F:I\times\mathbb{H}^n\to\mathbb{H}^n$. By a "discontinuous QDE" we mean any of the following: (i) an impulsive QDE, where solutions experience prescribed jumps $x(t_k^+)-x(t_k^-)=I_k(x(t_k^-))$ at a sequence of impulse instants $\{t_k\}$; (ii) a switched QDE $\dot x(t)=F_{\sigma(t)}(t,x(t))$ governed by a piecewise-constant switching signal $\sigma$; (iii) a QDE on a time scale $\mathbb{T}\subseteq\mathbb{R}$; (iv) a piecewise QDE whose right-hand side is defined piecewise on a partition of state or time space; or (v) a fuzzy-system QDE in which $F$ is determined by a fuzzy rule base. By a "discontinuous control scheme" for such a system we mean a feedback law $u$ entering $F$ that is itself impulsive, switching, time-scale-based, piecewise, or fuzzy.

Develop a unified theory of discontinuous QDEs of the above types that establishes, for each class, well-posedness (existence and uniqueness of solutions in an appropriate sense), stability criteria, and constructive controllability/stabilization results via discontinuous control. In particular, determine whether each discontinuous control strategy known for real-valued discontinuous ordinary differential equations (impulsive control, switching control, time-scale control, piecewise feedback, fuzzy control) can be adapted to its quaternion-valued counterpart, taking into account the noncommutativity of quaternion multiplication, and provide explicit conditions under which such adaptations yield asymptotic or exponential stabilization of the controlled discontinuous QDE.
artifact.category_tag: Quaternion-valued differential equations and discontinuous control
artifact.status_search_result: Several recent works have addressed parts of this program: basic theory and stability of impulsive quaternion-valued linear systems, controllability and observability of linear and nonlinear quaternion-valued impulsive differential equations, and discontinuous/fixed-time control of quaternion-valued (memristive) neural networks with discontinuous activations. These results cover impulsive and certain discontinuous-feedback subclasses, but a fully unified theory encompassing all of impulsive, switching, time-scale, piecewise, and fuzzy quaternion-valued discontinuous systems and their associated discontinuous control strategies has not been achieved. Hence the broad question is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Controllability and Observability Results for Quaternion-Valued Impulsive Differential Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Controllability and observability criteria for linear and nonlinear quaternion-valued impulsive differential equations.
status_evidence.claim: Impulsive QDE control theory has been partially developed.

status_evidence.title: Stability of Quaternion-Valued Impulsive Differential Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Sufficient criteria for asymptotic stability of linear QIDEs via impulsive Cauchy matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Stability theory for impulsive QDEs has been established.

status_evidence.title: Basic Theory of Impulsive Quaternion-Valued Linear Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational theory for impulsive quaternion-valued linear systems.

status_evidence.title: Fixed-Time Control for Memristor-Based Quaternion-Valued Neural Networks with Discontinuous Activation Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Discontinuous sign-function-based control for quaternion-valued networks with discontinuous activations.
status_evidence.claim: Discontinuous control strategies have been adapted to specific quaternion-valued settings.
